summary:
No Coquimbo-specific legal provision on gender identity, marriage, civil unions or hate-crime protection appears in the sources reviewed. Those matters are governed by Chilean national law and apply in the region as they do elsewhere in the country; the national record carries that layer.

Movilh's 24th annual report on sexual and gender diversity (HECHOS 2025, published March 2026) records Coquimbo at 2.62% of the abuse cases and complaints documented nationally, with the region's figure up 17.6% in 2025 on the previous year. That figure is a share of a national total and a count of complaints made to a civil-society organisation; it is not a per-capita rate, and it does not measure incidents that go unreported.

Nothing in the sources reviewed documents a Coquimbo-specific prosecution, court ruling, police practice or institutional policy concerning transgender people, and no regional enforcement pattern can be described from them.
tangentialFactors:
The region's only trans-relevant data point comes from a voluntary civil-society reporting system rather than an official statistical series. A rise in documented cases can reflect greater willingness to report, the presence of an organisation collecting complaints, or both, as much as a rise in underlying incidents.

Movilh reads the growth in regional shares of documented abuse as hatred spreading into areas where public debate over sexual and gender diversity is thinner. That is the compiling organisation's interpretation of the pattern, not an independent measurement, and it concerns the distribution of reporting across the country rather than conditions unique to Coquimbo.
localsOnly:
No region-specific service, remedy or administrative procedure for transgender residents in Coquimbo was identified in the sources reviewed. Complaints of discrimination and abuse from the region are recorded through a national civil-society reporting system, not through a regional institution of its own.

The 2.62% share of nationally documented cases is the only Coquimbo-specific figure the sources provide on residents' experience of discrimination.
outOfScopeNotes:
The 2024 baseline share used for the year-on-year comparison is not reproduced in the 2025 edition of the Movilh report, so the reported 17.6% change for Coquimbo cannot be verified from that edition alone.

The source gives no regional population denominator, so whether Coquimbo's 2.62% share of documented cases represents a rate above, below or level with the national average is not established.

National-level legal, budgetary and policy developments, and enforcement data for other regions, are outside this record's scope and are carried by the national assessment.
